from.place: the homotopy-colimit construction used before the final comparison: identify the cone of 1-shift with the termwise filtered colimit

title: Telescope homotopy colimits are termwise filtered colimits
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site, $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$, and let $E_0^\bullet\to E_1^\bullet\to\cdots$ be a sequence of cochain complexes of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. Define its homotopy colimit as the cone of $1-\operatorname{shift}:\bigoplus_n E_n^\bullet\to\bigoplus_n E_n^\bullet$. The canonical map from this homotopy colimit to the termwise filtered colimit $\varinjlim_n E_n^\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules].

source.place: Cohomology on Sites, Section 21.17, the telescope/colimit argument in Lemma 06YS

proof.text: Let u = telescopeShift and q = telescopeToColimit. On summand n the composite u q is colimit.ι_n minus E(n≤n+1) followed by colimit.ι_(n+1), hence zero by the colimit cocone identity.

Construct the cokernel cofork of u with projection q. A cofork p annihilating u gives maps a_n = ι_n p satisfying a_n = E(n≤n+1)a_(n+1). Induction extends this relation to every n≤m, so the a_n form a cocone. The colimit universal property supplies the unique factorization through q, verified on coproduct injections. The Lean helper telescope_cokernel carries this explicit construction.
Use lem-pc-telescope-shift-mono for monicity of u. The cokernel cofork from step 2 makes q epic and the short complex (u,q) exact, so the resulting sequence is short exact.

Apply lem-pc-cone-short-exact-quasi-iso to the resulting short exact sequence. Its actual morphism is mappingCone.descShortComplex, whose unshifted restriction is q and whose shifted cochain restriction is zero. Mathlib inr_descShortComplex and inl_desc give the two required identities. This proves the original existential with its canonicality clauses unchanged.
